title: Intrusive memories and dissociative phenomena during Video-EEG-monitoring
summary:
The occurrence of intrusive memories will be investigated in patients that undergo diagnostics for seizures and seizure-like episodes in an epilepsy clinic. In addition, so-called dissociative phenomena will be examined, which describe a splitting off of thoughts, feelings, memories and body movements from conscious perception.

The video-EEG method already allows the simultaneous recording of the external, observable signs of seizures and seizure-like episodes as well as a measurement of the electrical activity of the heart (ECG) and brain (EEG). Patients with epileptic seizures and patients with dissociative seizures can be reliably distinguished by this method. A third group consists of patients with cardiovascular episodes; other episodes can also be observed and differentiated from one another (e.g. panic attacks, impulsive outbursts or tic-disorders).
Since spontaneous episodes do not always occur during the inpatient stay, they can also be triggered by the hospital staff for diagnostic purposes using various provocation maneuvers.

The aim of this study is to supplement the proven video EEG method with a structured recording of subjective experience and a measurement of skin conductivity. This is intended to provide a clearer picture of the frequency of intrusive memories and the temporal connection to dissociative episodes. In addition, the roles of subjective experience and of the autonomic nervous system in various seizures and seizure-like episodes are to be examined more closely. Furthermore, the interpretation of EEG measurements during intrusive memories and dissociative symptoms should also be facilitated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with dissociative and functional disorders: Adult patients up to and including the age of 65 with diagnoses in the field of affective disorders (ICD-10 F30-F39), neurotic, stress and somatoform disorders (ICD-10 F40-F48) , personality and behavioral disorders (ICD-10 F60-F69) and/or behavioral and emotional disorders of childhood and adolescence onset (ICD-10 F90-F98). 

Patients with neurological diseases: Adult patients up to and including 65 years of age with diagnoses in the areas of inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system (ICD-10 G00-G09), extrapyramidal diseases and movement disorders (ICD-10 G20-G26), episodic and paroxysmal diseases of the central nervous system (ICD-10 G40-G47) and/or with symptoms affecting the nervous system and the musculoskeletal system (ICD-10 R25-R29). 

Patients with syncopal seizures: Adult patients up to and including 65 years of age with a diagnosis of syncope and collapse (ICD-10 R55) and/or other and unspecified seizures (ICD-10 R56.8). 

Conduction of a medically indicated video EEG examination. 
Availability of a smartphone.
Exclusion criteria:
Younger than 18 or older than 65 years, lack of capacity to give consent, acute suicidality, previous brain surgery (exceptions: implantation of deep electrodes, epilepsy surgery).
Certain infectious and parasitic diseases (ICD-10 A00-B99), malignant tumor diseases (ICD-10 C00-C97), organic mental disorders (ICD-10 F00-F09), serious mental and behavioral disorders caused by psychotropic substances (from ICD-10 F10 -F19), schizophrenia, schizotypy and delusional disorders (ICD-10 F20-F29), Intellectual disorders (ICD-10 F70-F79), severe developmental disorders (from ICD-10 F80-F89), system atrophies primarily affecting the central nervous system (ICD-10 G10-G14), other degenerative diseases of the nervous system (ICD-10 G30-G32 ), cerebrovascular diseases (ICD-10 I60-I69), pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum. (ICD-10 ICD-10 O00-O99).
